model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms generated by a language model, comparing the performance of the base model (Mistralv0.2-Base, shown in light blue) against versions fine-tuned on five medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics (represented by varying shades of orange and brown). The horizontal axis lists the six specialties, while the vertical axis represents the negative log probability on a linear scale ranging from -22 to -27. Each specialty group contains seven bars: one for the base model and six for the fine-tuned models (one per specialty). The bars are arranged such that the base model’s bar is positioned first in each group, followed by the fine-tuned models in the order: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics (as indicated by the legend). The height of each bar corresponds to the negative log probability value, with lower values (more negative) indicating better performance. For example, in the "Cardio" group, the base model’s bar reaches approximately -22.5, while the fine-tuned Cardio model’s bar reaches about -26.5, indicating improved performance. Similarly, in the "Pediatrics" group, the base model’s bar is around -22.5, whereas the fine-tuned Pediatrics model’s bar reaches approximately -25.5. The chart shows that fine-tuned models generally achieve lower negative log probabilities (i.e., higher likelihood) for terms within their respective specialty, with the most significant improvements observed when the model is fine-tuned on the same specialty as the test terms. The bars are not sorted by value but are grouped by specialty, and no visual emphasis (such as shading or annotations) is applied to any specific bar.
